# Built-in themes

A keep's **theme** decides what its files are: which kinds of item to make, what details each has, how items hold or relate to each other, and which searches, pages, thumbnails, and commands to offer. You choose it when you make a keep.

| Theme | For | Makes |
|---|---|---|
| [Files](files.md) | any folder | one item per file |
| [2D assets](assets2d.md) | art packs, game assets, fonts | artists holding images, fonts, and archives |
| [Music](music.md) | audio files with tags | artists ⊃ albums ⊃ songs |
| [Movies](movies.md) | video files, Kodi/Plex style | collections ⊃ movies, with their cast |
| [Books](books.md) | ebooks, comics, stories, documents | books and comics, their writers and artists, series, universes, collections |
| [Research](research.md) | papers, preprints, theses | papers with their authors in order, venues, projects |

What every theme shares:

- **Your files are never changed** (except by [Write to file…](../guide/write-to-file.md), which only the Books theme offers, and only where you allow it).
- **Tags, searches, Triage, Dedupe, undo** work the same everywhere.
- **Values you edit stay yours:** scans never change them.
- **Files can be versions:** where an item has several files (a song as MP3 and FLAC, a book bought from two stores, a paper's preprint and published version), they're one item.

Want a theme for something else (recipes, photos with sidecars, sheet music)? Themes are one Python file each: see [the theme guide](../THEMES.md).
